about: Changes of view through the chart's API and the viewport events they make, as the engine and the Python package both keep them: each case a chart (its portable spec over data, as contracts.json gives specs data) and actions in order. setViewport takes view (an x pair, an object of x, y, yRight, or null) and panel; it makes the events listed, in order (none when it changes nothing), or throws error (its ChartError's code, path, panel, and message), changing nothing. getViewport returns what returns says. update replaces the table's columns with data, fields keeping their kinds (Table.reset), and its events are those the next frame makes, of cause data; load gives the chart the options its spec makes over data (chart.update), as when fields change kinds, and its events are the next frame's, of cause options. remount mounts a chart in its place, of spec (or the case's) over data (or the case's): it takes the state viewportStatePayload gives of the chart before (restoreViewportState), its events are the restoration's, of cause options (none when nothing changes), and later actions act on it; placeholders name its instances afresh, and its revisions count from 1. Events are the JSON viewportEventPayload makes (web/events.ts): instance names are opaque, so they are written as placeholders ($x): in a case, a placeholder of a scale stands for one name of that scale's, and two placeholders of a scale for two (instances of different scales may share a name). scopes give each scale's scope in the case (insets keep scales of their own beside "chart"). Read by packages/herceg/test/web/viewport-events.test.ts (its shape), packages/herceg/test/browser/viewport-events.test.ts (every case through a chart), and Python's live tests.

cases.name: one panel: each change is one event, a reset of both axes one too, and a reset of nothing none
a time axis: views in epoch milliseconds, the scale and the panel's x marked as times
a view past the extent is moved inside with its span, and reported as shown
subplots sharing x, each with its own y: a panel names the y it zooms; the panels sharing x follow

error.message: setViewport y: the panels have y scales of their own; name one with { panel }
setViewport y: the panels have y scales of their own; name one with { panel }
setViewport: no panel "zz"; name one of "a", "b"

cases.name: subplots sharing y, each with its own x: one y range moves both, once

error.message: setViewport x: the panels have x scales of their own; name one with { panel }

cases.name: right y axes of panels' own: set apart from the left, reset with it, and refused where a panel has no such axis

error.message: setViewport yRight: panel "b" has no right y axis; drop yRight
setViewport y: panel "c" has no left y axis; drop y

cases.name: facet panels with y scales of their own, sharing x: a y range names its panel, an x range none

error.message: setViewport y: the panels have y scales of their own; name one with { panel }

cases.name: a facet panel whose rows go: its zoomed y is reported fitted with the panel it had, the x every panel shares keeps its view, and the panel comes back with that x and its own y unzoomed
facet panels that wrap anew share y with other panels: the zoomed y of the row they left is reported fitted, though every panel is still drawn
a panel's x scale whose numbers become categories is another instance: the zoomed one is reported fitted, though the panel stays
an inset's own scales beside the chart's x: its views leave its parent's alone, an x range without a panel is the parent's, and a reset resets both

error.message: setViewport y: the panels have y scales of their own; name one with { panel }

cases.name: a category x axis does not zoom: a range is refused, a reset is nothing to report

error.message: setViewport x: the x axis shows categories, which do not zoom; drop x

cases.name: a remount with a panel gone and back: the x every panel shares keeps its view, and a panel's own y keeps its view while it is drawn
a remount whose panels share the y they each had: the shared y is another instance, and stays fitted
a remount with a log y and limits on x: x keeps its view, moved inside the limits; y, of another type, stays fitted
a remount of facets with a panel's rows gone and back: x keeps its view, and the panel still drawn keeps its own y
